subject: Rapid burst readiness recap + metrics request
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Lena Brooks <lena@brightfin.com>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@brightfin.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Rapid burst readiness recap + metrics request

Hi Lena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and our proposed next steps so we can lock down an SLO & pilot plan: 

Call highlights / confirmed targets
- Streaming p95 token latency target: <= 250 ms
- Streaming p99 token latency target: <= 500 ms
- Baseline steady concurrency: 400 concurrent sessions (you reported this as normal daytime load)
- Expected burst concurrency: up to 1600 (4x baseline) for short windows (~2–8 minutes)
- Target autoscale ramp: reach 4x within 60s from baseline under sustained ramping traffic
- Warm pool objective: reduce cold-start tail — goal is pre-warmed capacity to cover ~20% of expected peak (~320 instances/equivalent slots)

Key open questions we need to quantify (items for action)
1) Peak composition: what fraction of burst traffic is streaming (longer sessions) vs short generations? This affects KV cache effectiveness.
2) Acceptable queueing behavior: prefer queueing up to X seconds (you suggested 30s) vs immediate 429/drop beyond headroom?
3) Billing & accounting: how do you want warm pool to be invoiced (reserved vs usage)?
4) Telemetry: confirm which metrics you need during the pilot (p95/p99 latency, GPUs active, queue depth, avg token/sec, KV hit rate).

Proposed immediate next steps
- Action A (redwood): share a minimal test plan + PoC config by EOD tomorrow. Will include warm pool sizing options (20%/30%/50% of peak) and scale-up policies (conservative vs aggressive). Attachment: BrightFin-SLOs-and-traffic-matrix.xlsx (your traffic numbers + our suggested mapping).
- Action B (BrightFin): confirm queueing preference and provide sample 10-minute trace or synthetic profile if available.
- Action C (both): schedule a 2-hour pilot kickoff next week to validate a targeted baseline->burst scenario.

I've attached an XLSX with the traffic matrix we discussed; Vanessa will follow up with a short proposal (config + rough cost delta for warm pool options).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: BrightFin-SLOs-and-traffic-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42 KB)

From: Lena Brooks <lena@brightfin.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@brightfin.com>, procurement@brightfin.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rapid burst readiness recap + metrics request

Aditya —

Thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Baseline 400 concurrency is accurate for weekdays; we see short spikes to ~700 occasionally. The large bursts (~1600) are typically marketing-driven and happen for 3–10 minutes.
- Composition: roughly 70% of requests during bursts are short text completions (avg tokens < 30), 30% are streaming sessions (multi-turn, avg duration ~45s).
- Queueing: we prefer a small buffer (queue up to 20s) rather than hard drops; client-side backoff is acceptable if you can expose a clear retry guidance.
- Billing: procurement asked whether warm pool capacity can be billed as a flat reserved monthly fee for the pilot window, instead of pay-as-you-go, to make forecasting simpler. Please include a reserved vs usage comparison.

Procurement (cc'd) will confirm the earliest contract window once we have a short pilot scope and cost delta.

I'll try to pull a short 10-minute capture from last week's campaign and share — should help tune the pilot.

—Lena
Lena Brooks
VP Product, BrightFin

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Lena Brooks <lena@brightfin.com>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@brightfin.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Rapid burst readiness recap + metrics request

On Wed, Jun 22, 2026 at 1:04 PM Lena Brooks <lena@brightfin.com> wrote:
> Aditya —
> 
> Thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
> - Baseline 400 concurrency is accurate...

Great questions — here is a concise pilot proposal and proposed config that maps to your asks: 

Pilot configuration (2-week PoC)
- Baseline target: configure service to sustain 400 concurrent sessions with p95 <= 250 ms
- Warm pool: 320 pre-warmed slots (20% of expected peak); optionally test 480 (30%) for a single validation run
- Autoscale policy: fast policy to add up to 3x baseline within 60s, and full 4x within 180s under aggressive ramp (gradual ramp policy tested separately)
- Queueing policy: allow queueing up to 20s, then apply 429 with a Retry-After header — we will expose client-side guidance and SDK error enums
- Metric surface: p50/p95/p99 token latency (stream and non-stream), active backends, queue depth, KV cache hit rate, kernel GPU utilization, scale-up latency. We will ship a Grafana dashboard link for the kickoff.

Test plan highlights
1) Synthetic ramp test: reproduce a 0->1600 concurrency ramp in 90s and measure time to reach 90% of target and tail latency.
2) Mixed load test: 70% short completions / 30% streams at 1600 concurrency for 5 minutes to validate KV and streaming behavior.
3) Cold-start run: disable warm pool and measure tail latency and drop rate.

Commercial notes
- We can present two billing options for the pilot: (A) reserved warm pool for pilot window (flat fee credited toward committed volume if you convert), (B) usage billing with line-item for warm pool instance-hours. I'll include a simple delta table in the proposal PDF.

Next operational asks (Aditya / BrightFin)
- Can you share the short trace Lena mentioned prior to the kickoff?
- Confirm pilot kickoff availability (we suggested Jun 29 or 30).

I'll attach the proposal (redwood-proposal-v1.pdf) with configuration and cost deltas. If this mapping looks good I suggest we lock in Jun 29 09:00 PT for a 2-hour kickoff.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)

From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@brightfin.com>

Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00

Vanessa / Aditya —

Thanks — proposal looks reasonable. Two quick clarifications before we lock the kickoff: 
1) If queueing hits 20s, will clients receive structured errors that our SDK can interpret to surface a friendly retry? We need clear error enums for mobile clients.
2) For the reserved warm pool pilot fee: procurement prefers reserved billing for the pilot window with a credit toward committed spend if we move to a 12‑month Dedicated contract. Please include an example invoice line.

We can do Jun 29 09:00 PT for the kickoff. Procurement will start paperwork once they see the invoice example. Lena — I’ll upload the 10-minute capture by EOD.

—Tom
Tom Hsu
Engineering Lead, BrightFin
